mishnayos.summary: An erech is never less than one sela and never more than fifty. The mishnah then lists other things in the Torah that have a smallest and a biggest number.

chunks.en: For an erech, no one pays less than one sela,
chunks.explain: A poor person pays what he can, but at least one sela.

words.note: A silver coin.

chunks.en: and no one pays more than fifty sela'im.
How so? If a poor person gave one sela and later became rich,
he does not have to give anything more.
If he gave less than a sela and then became rich,
he must give fifty sela'im.
If the poor person had five sela'im,
Rabbi Meir says,
he gives only one.
And the Chachamim say,
he gives all of them.
For an erech, no one pays less than one sela,
and no one pays more than fifty sela'im.

chunks.stMore: Normally a newborn is circumcised on his eighth day. If he was born during twilight, which an uncertain period of day or night, he is circumcised on what would be the eighth day of his birth if he is was born at night, which is the ninth day if he was born during the day. If he was born during twilight on Shabbat eve, the circumcision cannot be performed on Friday, as he might have been born on Shabbat and therefore Friday is only the seventh day. And the circumcision cannot be on Shabbat, as perhaps he was born on Friday and only circumcision performed on the eighth day overrides Shabbat. Therefore, it is postponed until after Shabbat. If two days of Rosh HaShana occur on Sunday and Monday, the circumcision is postponed until Tuesday, the twelfth day after birth.
